export.title: Wikimedia Sightglass export
info.intro: Wikimedia Sightglass helps you explore Wikimedia's mediacounts dataset, which tracks how often Wikimedia Commons files are loaded. Queries can be run on individual files or category trees. Queries run serverside and the results for categories may be saved for later reference and sharing.
info.background1: Commons contributors often want to know how many views their media receives, and for GLAM institutions it's one of the main ways to measure impact.
info.background2: The community measures media views in two ways: by the view stats for pages a file appears on and/or by how often the files themselves are loaded. Each approach has trade-offs.
info.background3: For counting article pageviews: Tools like GLAMorgan surface this data, but only for current usage. Once a file is removed from a page, that past usage drops out of later queries. Other tools such as Commons Impact Metrics store pageview data over time, but this requires opt-in setup and can still miss short bursts (e.g. a file is added to the Wikipedia front page for a day and receives millions of views).
info.background4: For counting media file loads: The Wikimedia Foundation provides mediacount stats, which track how often individual files are loaded over time. These counts can be inflated by bots, scrapers, and browser preloading, but they capture historic usage and short-lived bursts, so they can paint a fuller picture for impact analysis.
info.background5: Sightglass was made to help Wikimedia users query and share those latter mediacount stats. Especially when used alongside article usage and pageview data, this helps give a comprehensive picture of media impact.
info.how1: The mediacounts dataset records how often Commons files are transferred to users. Bots, scrapers, and browser prefetching can inflate the numbers; the Wikimedia Foundation filters out much of this traffic, but some still gets through.
info.how2: For more detail, see the Wikitech documentation.
